questions.question: A military camp has provisions for 360 soldiers for 50 days. After 10 days, 120 more soldiers arrive at the camp. Assuming the daily consumption per soldier remains constant, for how many more days will the remaining provisions last?
questions.solution: [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__ Remaining food is sufficient for **360 soldiers** for **40 days** (50 − 10). Total soldiers after arrival = 360 + 120 = **480 soldiers**. Using **M₁D₁ = M₂D₂** logic on remaining stock: 360 × 40 = 480 × Days. Days = 14400 ÷ 480 = **30 days**. **∴ The correct answer is 30 days.**

questions.question: What is the mean proportional between 0.0009 and 0.25?
questions.solution: [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__ The **Mean Proportional** between two numbers **a** and **b** is calculated as **√(a × b)**. Given **a = 0.0009** and **b = 0.25**. Mean proportional = √(0.0009 × 0.25) = 0.03 × 0.5 = 0.015. **∴ The correct answer is 0.015.**

questions.question:
A car travels the first 60 km at 45 km/hr and the next 90 km at 60 km/hr. What is the average speed for the entire journey?

(Round off your answer to two decimal places.)
questions.solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

**Average Speed** = (D₁ + D₂) ÷ (D₁/S₁ + D₂/S₂)

Average Speed = (60 + 90) ÷ (60/45 + 90/60)

Average Speed = 150 ÷ (4/3 + 3/2) = 150 ÷ (17/6)

Average Speed = 900 ÷ 17 ≈ 52.94 km/hr

**∴ The correct answer is 52.94 km/hr.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

First distance (d₁) = 60 km | Speed (s₁) = 45 km/hr

Second distance (d₂) = 90 km | Speed (s₂) = 60 km/hr

**Formula Used:**

**Average Speed** = Total Distance ÷ Total Time

Time = Distance ÷ Speed

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ff14ef168d26e9f749995ef16349198b8d3f269bbac40fc4c5f9b631c83ac9d4.png] 

**Calculations:**

⇒ **Time** taken for the first part (t₁) = 60 ÷ 45 = 4/3 hours

⇒ **Time** taken for the second part (t₂) = 90 ÷ 60 = 3/2 hours

⇒ **Total Time** = t₁ + t₂ = 4/3 + 3/2

⇒ **Total Time** = (8 + 9) ÷ 6 = 17/6 hours

⇒ **Total Distance** = 60 + 90 = 150 km

⇒ **Average Speed** = 150 ÷ (17/6) = (150 × 6) ÷ 17

⇒ **Average Speed** = 900 ÷ 17 = 52.9411... km/hr

**∴ The correct answer is 52.94 km/hr.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Average Speed for Equal Distances

If a body travels two equal distances at speeds x and y, the average speed is given by (2 × x × y) ÷ (x + y).

Average Speed for Equal Time Intervals

If a body travels at speeds x and y for equal time intervals, the average speed is simply the arithmetic mean: (x + y) ÷ 2.

Relative Speed Concept

For objects moving in the same direction, relative speed = S₁ − S₂. For opposite directions, relative speed = S₁ + S₂.

questions.question: The sum of two positive numbers is 36 and their product is 180. The positive difference between them is:
questions.solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

The **Shortcut formula** to find the **Difference** when **Sum** and **Product** are given:

**Difference² = Sum² − 4 × Product**

⇒ Difference² = 36² − 4 × 180

⇒ Difference² = 1296 − 720 = 576

⇒ Difference = √576 = 24

**∴ The correct answer is 24.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

Sum of two **Positive Numbers** (x + y) = 36

Product of the numbers (xy) = 180

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/5f61862534f841a6ce0dfa0abdf2e54ab478a11e1cbe345817b2e866b14ef991.png] 

**Formula Used:** (x − y)² = (x + y)² − 4xy

⇒ (x − y)² = (36)² − 4 × 180

⇒ (x − y)² = 1296 − 720

⇒ (x − y)² = 576

⇒ x − y = √576

⇒ x − y = 24

**∴ The correct answer is 24.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Algebraic Identities

(x + y)² = x² + y² + 2xy and (x − y)² = x² + y² − 2xy. Subtracting these gives (x + y)² − (x − y)² = 4xy.

Finding Individual Numbers

If Sum (S) and Difference (D) are known, the larger number is (S + D) ÷ 2 and the smaller number is (S − D) ÷ 2.

Sum of Squares

The sum of squares of two numbers can be found using x² + y² = (x + y)² − 2xy.

questions.question: The sides of a triangle are 75 cm, 21 cm, and 72 cm. What is the length (in cm) of its altitude corresponding to the side with a length of 21 cm?
questions.solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

Check the ratio of the sides: 75 : 21 : 72 ÷ 3 = 25 : 7 : 24.

The numbers 7, 24, and 25 form a **Pythagorean triplet**, which means the triangle is **right-angled**.

In a **right-angled triangle**, the **altitude** corresponding to one leg is simply the length of the other leg.

The sides forming the right angle are 21 cm and 72 cm.

**∴ The correct answer is 72 cm.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:** The sides of the **triangle** are 75 cm, 21 cm, and 72 cm.

**Formula Used:** Area of a triangle = (1 ÷ 2) × base × altitude

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4166244c1ddcc3e3d7fab512facf4023aff6b636871eb7b9eac8b62a2bf2ad07.png] 

⇒ First, identify the type of triangle using the **Pythagoras Theorem**: 21² + 72² = 441 + 5184 = 5625.

⇒ Since 75² = 5625, the sides satisfy a² + b² = c², making it a **right-angled triangle**.

⇒ In this triangle, the longest side (75 cm) is the **hypotenuse**, and the other two sides (21 cm and 72 cm) are the **legs** (base and perpendicular).

⇒ **Area** = (1 ÷ 2) × product of legs = (1 ÷ 2) × 21 × 72.

⇒ Also, **Area** = (1 ÷ 2) × base (21 cm) × altitude (h).

⇒ (1 ÷ 2) × 21 × 72 = (1 ÷ 2) × 21 × h.

⇒ h = 72 cm.

**∴ The correct answer is 72 cm.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Pythagorean Triplets

Sets of three positive integers a, b, and c, such that a² + b² = c². Common triplets include (3, 4, 5), (5, 12, 13), and (7, 24, 25).

Altitude of a Right Triangle

The two legs of a right-angled triangle act as altitudes to each other. The altitude to the hypotenuse can be found using: (Leg₁ × Leg₂) ÷ Hypotenuse.

Heron's Formula

For any triangle with sides a, b, and c, Area = √(s × (s − a) × (s − b) × (s − c)), where semi-perimeter s = (a + b + c) ÷ 2.

questions.question: The average age of 7 students in a class is 17 years. When a new student join the class, the average age of the class becomes 18 years. Find the age of the new student.
questions.solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

**Age of new student** = New Average + (Initial count of students × Increase in average)

⇒ Increase in **Average Age** = 18 − 17 = 1 year

⇒ Age = 18 + (7 × 1) = 25 years

**∴ The correct answer is 25 years.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

Initial number of **students** = 7

Initial **average age** = 17 years

New **average age** = 18 years

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/9c9e9408dc1425aee2dd0b2760aa00973fd30064c0e0e38006728171f0b93940.png] 

**Formula Used:**

Total Age = Average Age × Number of Students

**Calculations:**

⇒ Total age of 7 **students** = 7 × 17 = 119 years

⇒ Total number of **students** after 1 joins = 8

⇒ Total age of 8 **students** = 8 × 18 = 144 years

⇒ Age of **new student** = Total age of 8 students − Total age of 7 students

⇒ Age = 144 − 119

⇒ Age = 25 years

**∴ The correct answer is 25 years.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Basic Average Formula

The **Average** of a set of numbers is the sum of the values divided by the total number of values: Average = (Sum of observations) ÷ (Total number of observations).

Effect of Adding a Constant

If a **constant value** 'k' is added to each observation in a data set, the original average also increases by exactly 'k'.

Weighted Average

When two groups with different averages are combined, the **combined average** is (n₁x₁ + n₂x₂) ÷ (n₁ + n₂), where n is the count and x is the average of each group.

questions.question: Find the volume of a cylinder whose height is 21 cm and its radius is 3/5 of the radius of another cylinder with a volume of 317900 cm³ and a height of 14 cm. (Use π = 22/7)
questions.solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

Ratio of **volumes** of two cylinders: V₁/V₂ = (r₁/r₂)² × (h₁/h₂)

V₁ = 317900 × (3/5)² × (21/14)

V₁ = 317900 × (9/25) × (3/2) = 317900 × (27/50)

V₁ = 6358 × 27 = 171666 cm³

**∴ The correct answer is 171666 cm³.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

**Height** of first cylinder (h₁) = 21 cm

**Volume** of second cylinder (V₂) = 317900 cm³

**Height** of second cylinder (h₂) = 14 cm

**Radius** of first cylinder (r₁) = 3/5 × radius of second cylinder (r₂)

**Formula Used:** Volume of cylinder = πr²h

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/13ba88599b2173c5112a7951b3c98cea1d1dee70624e06eda1a1bb06d48db048.png] 

**Calculations:**

⇒ Volume of second cylinder (V₂) = π × r₂² × h₂

⇒ 317900 = (22/7) × r₂² × 14

⇒ 317900 = 22 × r₂² × 2

⇒ 317900 = 44 × r₂²

⇒ r₂² = 317900 ÷ 44 = 7225

⇒ r₂ = √7225 = 85 cm

⇒ Radius of first cylinder (r₁) = 3/5 × 85 = 3 × 17 = 51 cm

⇒ Volume of first cylinder (V₁) = π × r₁² × h₁

⇒ V₁ = (22/7) × (51)² × 21

⇒ V₁ = 22 × 2601 × 3

⇒ V₁ = 66 × 2601 = 171666 cm³

**∴ The correct answer is 171666 cm³.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Curved Surface Area of Cylinder

The area of the curved surface is given by the formula CSA = 2πrh.

Total Surface Area of Cylinder

The sum of the areas of the curved surface and the two circular bases: TSA = 2πr(h + r).

Volume and Ratio Property

If the radius and height of two cylinders are in the ratio r₁:r₂ and h₁:h₂, then the ratio of their volumes is (r₁/r₂)² × (h₁/h₂).

questions.question: If 45% of a number exceeds 20% of it by 36, then the number is:
questions.solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

Find the **percentage difference**: 45% − 20% = 25%.

The question states that 25% of the **number** is 36.

To get the **total number** (100%), multiply by 4 (since 25% × 4 = 100%).

Result = 36 × 4 = 144.

**∴ The correct answer is 144.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

First percentage = 45%

Second percentage = 20%

Difference in values = 36

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/e801ff53a60ad123b04fbe9fe965a892355a506fb2398c2b962a0d441e269cf1.png] 

**Calculations:**

⇒ Let the **number** be x.

⇒ According to the problem: 45% of x − 20% of x = 36

⇒ (45 − 20)% of x = 36

⇒ 25% of x = 36

⇒ (25 ÷ 100) × x = 36

⇒ (1 ÷ 4) × x = 36

⇒ x = 36 × 4

⇒ x = 144

**∴ The correct answer is 144.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Percentage Formula

The value of **P%** of a number **N** is calculated as **(P × N) ÷ 100**.

Finding the Base Number

If **x%** of a number is **V**, the original number is **(V ÷ x) × 100**.

Common Fraction Equivalents

Knowing common fractions like **20% = 1/5**, **25% = 1/4**, and **50% = 1/2** helps in faster calculation during competitive exams.

questions.question: Two taps can fill a cistern in 4 hours and 9 hours, respectively. A third tap can empty it in 9 hours. How long (in hours) will it take to fill one-fourth of the empty cistern if all the taps are opened together?
questions.solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

**Tap B** (fills in 9 hr) and **Tap C** (empties in 9 hr) have equal rates and opposite effects.

Their net **Efficiency** is zero, meaning only **Tap A** effectively fills the **cistern**.

**Tap A** takes 4 hr to fill the complete **cistern**.

Time to fill **one-fourth** of the **cistern** = 4 hr × 1/4 = 1 hr.

**∴ The correct answer is 1 hr.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

Time taken by **Tap A** = 4 hr

Time taken by **Tap B** = 9 hr

Time taken by **Tap C** (Emptying) = 9 hr

**Formula Used:**

**Efficiency** = **Total Work** ÷ **Time**

**Calculations:**

⇒ Total **Efficiency** of all **taps** = 9 + 4 − 4 = 9 units/hr.

⇒ Target to fill **one-fourth** of the **cistern** = 36 ÷ 4 = 9 units.

⇒ Time required = 9 units ÷ 9 units/hr = 1 hr.

**∴ The correct answer is 1 hr.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Inlet and Outlet Pipes

An inlet pipe fills the tank (positive efficiency), while an outlet pipe empties the tank (negative efficiency).

Net Efficiency

When multiple pipes work together, the net filling or emptying rate is the algebraic sum of their individual efficiencies.

LCM Method

The capacity of the tank is usually assumed to be the Least Common Multiple (LCM) of the individual time periods given in the problem.

questions.question: If on a sale, there is 40% discount on the marked price of ₹1,200, but the sale is done at ₹520 only, then how much additional discount did the customer get?
questions.solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

Price after **40% discount** = 60% of 1200 = ₹720.

Final **Sale Price** = ₹520.

**Additional Discount** value = 720 − 520 = ₹200.

Additional Discount % = (200 ÷ 720) × 100 = (5 ÷ 18) × 100 = 250/9% = 27(7)/(9)%.

**∴ The correct answer is 27(7)/(9)%.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

**Marked Price (MP)** = ₹1,200

**First Discount** = 40%

**Final Sale Price (SP)** = ₹520

**Formula:**

Price after discount = MP × (100 − Discount%) ÷ 100

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/2ce20f091a3eaa3a3b112d62504bfc75d8d13e34f1fadf714d3fbfaba2f473c3.png] 

**Calculations:**

⇒ Price after 40% discount = 1200 × (1 − 0.40)

⇒ Price after 40% discount = 1200 × 0.60 = ₹720

⇒ Total **Additional Discount** needed = 720 − 520 = ₹200

⇒ **Additional Discount %** = (Additional Discount ÷ Mid Price) × 100

⇒ Additional Discount % = (200 ÷ 720) × 100

⇒ Additional Discount % = (5 ÷ 18) × 100 = 500/18%

⇒ Additional Discount % = 250/9% = 27 7/9%

**∴ The correct answer is 27(7)/(9)%.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Successive Discounts

When two discounts a% and b% are given, the **equivalent single discount** is calculated as: [a + b − (ab ÷ 100)]%.

Marked Price (MP)

The price printed on the product. Discounts are always calculated on the **Marked Price** unless stated otherwise.

Selling Price (SP)

The actual price at which an item is sold after all discounts. SP = MP − **Discount**.

questions.question: If the interest on a sum of ₹y at 2% per annum compounded annually for 2 years is ₹404, then the total amount payable at the end of the two-year period will be _________.
questions.solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

Effective rate of **Compound Interest** for **2 years** at **2%** = 2 + 2 + (2 × 2)/100 = **4.04%**.

Given **Compound Interest** (4.04%) = **₹404**.

⇒ **Principal (y)** = (404 ÷ 4.04) × 100 = **₹10,000**.

**Total Amount** = Principal + Interest = 10,000 + 404 = **₹10,404**.

**∴ The correct answer is ₹10,404.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:** **Interest (CI)** = ₹404, **Rate (r)** = 2% per annum, **Time (n)** = 2 years.

**Formula Used:** Amount (A) = P(1 + r/100)ⁿ and CI = A − P

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/fdeff2dc8ecd219278a5ee70aac08458990382ae81c1f37fce027cf925880dc0.png] 

⇒ CI = y[(1 + 2/100)² − 1]

⇒ 404 = y[(51/50)² − 1]

⇒ 404 = y[2601/2500 − 1]

⇒ 404 = y[101/2500]

⇒ y = (404 × 2500) ÷ 101

⇒ y = 4 × 2500 = 10,000

⇒ **Total Amount (A)** = Principal (y) + Interest

⇒ **Total Amount (A)** = 10,000 + 404 = 10,404

**∴ The correct answer is ₹10,404.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Effective Percentage Rate

For two successive changes of a% and b%, the effective change is (a + b + ab/100)%.

CI vs SI Difference

The difference between **Compound Interest** and **Simple Interest** for 2 years is P(r/100)².

Amount Property

In **Compound Interest**, the **Total Amount** of the previous year becomes the **Principal** for the next year.

questions.question: Find the smallest natural number x, for which 2x + 1 is not a prime number.
questions.solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

A **natural number** is a positive integer starting from 1 (1, 2, 3, ...).

Evaluate the expression 2x + 1 sequentially:

For x = 1, 2, 3 → 2x + 1 = 3, 5, 7 (all are **prime numbers**)

For x = 4 → 2(4) + 1 = 9 (**composite number**, not prime)

**∴ The correct answer is 4.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

An algebraic expression: 2x + 1

We need to find the smallest **natural number** x such that 2x + 1 is not a **prime number**.

**Definition and Method:**

A **natural number** belongs to the set {1, 2, 3, 4, ...}.

A **prime number** is a positive integer greater than 1 that has no positive divisors other than 1 and itself.

We substitute sequential natural numbers for x into the expression and check for primality.

**Calculations:**

⇒ For x = 1:

⇒ 2(1) + 1 = 3 (Prime number)

⇒ For x = 2:

⇒ 2(2) + 1 = 5 (Prime number)

⇒ For x = 3:

⇒ 2(3) + 1 = 7 (Prime number)

⇒ For x = 4:

⇒ 2(4) + 1 = 9 (Composite number, since 9 = 3 × 3)

Since 9 is divisible by 3, it is not a prime number. Hence, the smallest natural number satisfying the given condition is x = 4.

**∴ The correct answer is 4.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Prime Numbers

A prime number is a positive integer greater than 1 that has exactly two distinct positive divisors: 1 and itself. Examples include 2, 3, 5, 7, 11, etc.

Composite Numbers

A composite number is a positive integer greater than 1 that has more than two distinct positive divisors. For example, 4, 6, 8, 9, 10 are composite numbers.

Natural Numbers

Natural numbers are the set of positive integers starting from 1, i.e., {1, 2, 3, 4, ...}. Note that 0 is not considered a natural number in this context.

Primality of 2x + 1

For any integer x, the expression 2x + 1 always represents an odd number. Thus, we are looking for the smallest odd composite number greater than 1, which is 9.

questions.question: If the sum of the ages of a father and son is 56 years and the father is 24 years older than his son, what is the son's age (in years)?
questions.solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

When the **sum (S)** and **difference (D)** of two ages are known:

**Son's age (Smaller value)** = (Sum − Difference) ÷ 2

Son's age = (56 − 24) ÷ 2

Son's age = 32 ÷ 2 = 16 years

**∴ The correct answer is 16 years.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

⇒ **Sum** of Father and Son's ages = 56 years

⇒ **Difference** between Father and Son's ages = 24 years

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/5fe9c18073922d29b268c5d794c8fcaef13a720c97f6b141da81125245fb744c.png] 

⇒ Let the age of the **son** be x years.

⇒ According to the question, the **father** is 24 years older than the son.

⇒ Father's age = (x + 24) years

⇒ Sum of their ages: x + (x + 24) = 56

⇒ 2x + 24 = 56

⇒ 2x = 56 − 24

⇒ 2x = 32

⇒ x = 32 ÷ 2

⇒ x = 16

**∴ The correct answer is 16 years.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Linear Equations in Ages

Age problems are typically solved by forming a **linear equation** where the unknown age is represented by a variable like 'x'.

Constant Age Difference

The difference between the ages of two individuals **never changes** over time. If the father is 24 years older now, he will always be 24 years older.

Sum and Difference Rule

If (A + B) = S and (A − B) = D, then the larger value A = (S + D) ÷ 2 and the smaller value B = (S − D) ÷ 2.

questions.question: Three numbers are in the ratio of 19 : 7 : 13, and their LCM is 8645. Their HCF is:
questions.solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

**Ratio** of numbers = 19 : 7 : 13

Since 19, 7, and 13 are all **prime numbers**, they are co-prime to each other.

For co-prime ratios, **LCM** = (Product of Ratios) × **HCF**

8645 = (19 × 7 × 13) × **HCF** ⇒ 8645 = 1729 × **HCF**

**HCF** = 8645 ÷ 1729 = 5

**∴ The correct answer is 5.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

**Ratio** of three numbers = 19 : 7 : 13

**Least Common Multiple (LCM)** = 8645

**Formula Used:**

Let the **HCF** be x. Then the numbers are ax, bx, and cx.

**LCM** of (ax, bx, cx) = x × **LCM**(a, b, c)

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/290a237e7f4c254defdcea3b5f48b3e2cb65f32a07a2d921feb34b36890f4275.png] 

**Calculations:**

⇒ Let the three numbers be 19x, 7x, and 13x, where **x** is the **HCF**.

⇒ Since 19, 7, and 13 are **prime numbers**, their **LCM** is the product of these numbers and their common factor x.

⇒ **LCM** = 19 × 7 × 13 × x

⇒ 8645 = 1729 × x

⇒ x = 8645 ÷ 1729

⇒ x = 5

Therefore, the **Highest Common Factor (HCF)** of the numbers is 5, which corresponds to **Option 4**.

**∴ The correct answer is 5.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Relationship between HCF and LCM

For any two numbers a and b, the product of the numbers is equal to the product of their HCF and LCM: a × b = HCF(a, b) × LCM(a, b).

HCF of Co-prime Numbers

The **HCF** of two or more **co-prime numbers** (numbers that have no common factor other than 1) is always 1.

LCM and HCF of Fractions

LCM of fractions = (LCM of Numerators) ÷ (HCF of Denominators). HCF of fractions = (HCF of Numerators) ÷ (LCM of Denominators).

questions.question: 15 men and 19 women can complete a piece of work in 8 days, and 9 men and 4 women can complete the same work in 14 days. The work of how many women is equivalent to that of one man?
questions.solution:

Equate the total work done in both cases: (**15M** + **19W**) × **8 days** = (**9M** + **4W**) × **14 days**.

Divide both sides by 2: (**15M** + **19W**) × 4 = (**9M** + **4W**) × 7.

Expand and group terms: 60M + 76W = 63M + 28W ⇒ 3M = 48W.

Thus, 1 man is equivalent to **16 women**.

questions.question: A shopkeeper buys sugar at ₹48 per kg. While selling, he uses a faulty weighing scale that gives only 960 g instead of 1 kg. In addition, he marks the selling price at a profit of 20% on the cost price and then offers a discount of 10% on the marked price. Find the overall percentage profit or loss made by the shopkeeper.
questions.solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

Net Profit Ratio = (True Weight ÷ Faulty Weight) × (Markup Factor) × (Discount Factor)

Net Ratio = (1000 ÷ 960) × (120 ÷ 100) × (90 ÷ 100)

Net Ratio = (25/24) × (6/5) × (9/10) = 45/40 = 9/8

Profit % = [(9 − 8) ÷ 8] × 100 = 1/8 × 100 = 12.5%

**∴ The correct answer is 12.5% profit.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

Cost Price (**CP**) per kg = ₹48

**Markup** percentage = 20%

**Discount** percentage = 10%

**Faulty weight** used = 960 g instead of 1000 g

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/982ce725a99c62f313285dbf62ec21f235477ac773a94054d5953a108d977f06.png] 

**Calculations:**

⇒ Marked Price (**MP**) for 1000 g = 48 + (20 ÷ 100) × 48 = 48 + 9.6 = ₹57.6

⇒ Selling Price (**SP**) for 1000 g = 57.6 − (10 ÷ 100) × 57.6 = 57.6 − 5.76 = ₹51.84

⇒ The shopkeeper delivers only 960 g, so his **actual cost** is for 960 g.

⇒ Actual CP for 960 g = (48 ÷ 1000) × 960 = 0.048 × 960 = ₹46.08

⇒ Total Profit = SP for 1000 g (received from customer) − Actual CP for 960 g

⇒ Total Profit = 51.84 − 46.08 = ₹5.76

⇒ Profit % = (Total Profit ÷ Actual CP) × 100

⇒ Profit % = (5.76 ÷ 46.08) × 100 = 1/8 × 100 = 12.5%

**∴ The correct answer is 12.5% profit.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Dishonest Dealer Formula

Profit % = [ (True Weight − False Weight) ÷ False Weight ] × 100 when selling at cost price.

Successive Discounts/Markups

Effective change of two percentages x and y is given by the formula: [ x + y + (xy ÷ 100) ].

General Profit Relation

Selling Price (SP) = CP × (100 + Profit%) ÷ 100 = MP × (100 − Discount%) ÷ 100.

questions.question: What will be the total amount payable after 3 years on a principal of ₹4,000 at 5% per annum, compounded annually?
questions.solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

Rate = **5%** = 1/20 → **Principal** : **Amount** ratio for 1 year = 20 : 21.

For **3 years**, Ratio = (20)³ : (21)³ = 8000 : 9261.

Given 8000 units = ₹4,000 ⇒ 1 unit = ₹0.5.

**Total Amount** = 9261 × 0.5 = ₹4,630.50.

**∴ The correct answer is ₹4,630.50.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

**Principal (P)** = ₹4,000

**Rate (R)** = 5% per annum

**Time (n)** = 3 years

**Formula Used:**

Amount (A) = P(1 + R/100)ⁿ

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/0f208508877e273ec4c4d7b922cdf94c809f18153f353df7f090eb47c371ef24.png] 

**Calculations:**

⇒ A = 4000 × (1 + 5/100)³

⇒ A = 4000 × (1 + 1/20)³

⇒ A = 4000 × (21/20)³

⇒ A = 4000 × (9261 / 8000)

⇒ A = 9261 / 2

⇒ A = ₹4,630.50

**∴ The correct answer is ₹4,630.50.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Compound Interest (CI) Formula

CI = P[(1 + R/100)ⁿ − 1], where P is Principal, R is Rate, and n is Time.

Difference between CI and SI for 3 Years

Difference = P(R/100)² × (3 + R/100). This formula helps find the gap between simple and compound interest quickly.

Successive Percentage Method

The effective rate for 5% over 3 years is calculated as [5 + 5 + (5×5)/100] = 10.25% for 2 years, then combining 10.25% and 5% to get 15.7625% for 3 years.

questions.question:
Simplify:

 (sin² A)/(1 - cos A) + (sin² A)/(1 + cos A)
questions.solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

Use the **Value Substitution Method** by assuming **A = 90°**.

At **A = 90°**, the values are **sin 90° = 1** and **cos 90° = 0**.

Substitute these into the expression: **(1²) / (1 − 0) + (1²) / (1 + 0)**.

⇒ **1 / 1 + 1 / 1 = 2**.

**∴ The correct answer is 2.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:** (sin² A) / (1 − cos A) + (sin² A) / (1 + cos A)

**Formula Used:** sin² A + cos² A = 1 ⇒ **sin² A = 1 − cos² A**

⇒ Factor out **sin² A**: sin² A [ 1 / (1 − cos A) + 1 / (1 + cos A) ]

⇒ Take the **LCM** inside the bracket: sin² A [ (1 + cos A + 1 − cos A) / ((1 − cos A)(1 + cos A)) ]

⇒ Simplify the numerator and apply **(a−b)(a+b) = a²−b²**: sin² A [ 2 / (1 − cos² A) ]

⇒ Substitute **1 − cos² A = sin² A**: sin² A [ 2 / sin² A ]

⇒ **2**

**∴ The correct answer is 2.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Fundamental Trigonometric Identities

The three primary identities are **sin²θ + cos²θ = 1**, **1 + tan²θ = sec²θ**, and **1 + cot²θ = cosec²θ**.

Algebraic Manipulations

Trigonometric expressions often utilize **a² − b² = (a − b)(a + b)**, such as **1 − cos² A = (1 − cos A)(1 + cos A)**.

Substitution Method

In objective exams, substituting standard angles like **0°, 30°, 45°, 60°, or 90°** can solve complex identities rapidly, provided the expression remains defined.

questions.question: A, B and C started a business, investing amounts of ₹1,960, ₹1,660, and ₹1,130 respectively. If B's share in the profit earned by them is ₹968, what is the difference in the profit (in ₹) earned by A and C?
questions.solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

Ratio of investments of **A : B : C** = 1960 : 1660 : 1130 = **196 : 166 : 113**.

Difference in profit shares of **A and C** = 196 − 113 = **83 units**.

Given, **B's share** = 166 units = **₹968**.

Since 83 is exactly **half** of 166, the required difference = 968 ÷ 2 = **₹484**.

**∴ The correct answer is ₹484.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

Investment of **A** = ₹1,960

Investment of **B** = ₹1,660

Investment of **C** = ₹1,130

Profit share of **B** = ₹968

**Formula Used:**

In a partnership, **Profit Ratio** = **Investment Ratio** × **Time Period** (where Time is same for all).

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/bb3ec140c0833325c31437263dda9f1ec29edb64bd34273bd0847dab7d1a7416.png] 

**Calculations:**

⇒ Ratio of profits of **A : B : C** = 1960 : 1660 : 1130

⇒ Ratio = **196 : 166 : 113**

⇒ Let the profits be 196x, 166x, and 113x respectively.

⇒ 166x = 968

⇒ x = 968 ÷ 166 = 484 ÷ 83

⇒ Difference in profit earned by **A and C** = 196x − 113x = **83x**

⇒ Difference = 83 × (484 ÷ 83)

⇒ Difference = **₹484**

**∴ The correct answer is ₹484.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Partnership Profit Sharing

Profit is distributed among partners in the ratio of (Investment₁ × Time₁) : (Investment₂ × Time₂). If the time period is equal, profit depends solely on the investment ratio.

Simple vs. Compound Partnership

In a simple partnership, all partners invest for the same duration. In a compound partnership, the duration of investments varies for different partners.

Active and Sleeping Partners

An active partner manages the business and may receive a fixed salary or a percentage of the profit before the remaining profit is distributed according to investment ratios.

questions.question: Chetan’s salary is ₹17,000 per month. He spends ₹4,000 on house rent, ₹2,500 on bills, and the rest of the amount is his monthly savings. Find his savings (in ₹) in a year, if in the month of his birthday, he spent his complete monthly savings for a birthday celebration.
questions.solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

Net monthly **savings** = 17,000 − (4,000 + 2,500) = ₹10,500.

Since the **savings** of the **birthday month** is spent entirely, effective saving occurs for 11 months.

Total **annual savings** = 10,500 × 11 = ₹1,15,500.

**∴ The correct answer is ₹1,15,500.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

Monthly **salary** of **Chetan** = ₹17,000

Monthly **house rent** = ₹4,000

Monthly **bills** = ₹2,500

**Formula Used:**

Monthly **savings** = Monthly **salary** − Total **expenditure**

Annual **savings** = Monthly **savings** × Number of months saved

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/6e6591403bbbbe57589a27d4ad407175b9c94fff7c81dfe91c660d9da127f141.png] 

**Calculations:**

⇒ Total monthly **expenditure** = 4,000 + 2,500 = ₹6,500

⇒ Monthly **savings** = 17,000 − 6,500 = ₹10,500

⇒ In the **birthday month**, **savings** = ₹0 (as he spent the complete amount for celebration)

⇒ Total months in a **year** = 12

⇒ Effective months for **savings** = 12 − 1 = 11 months

⇒ Total **savings** in a **year** = 10,500 × 11

⇒ Total **savings** = ₹1,15,500

**∴ The correct answer is ₹1,15,500.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Income and Savings Relationship

Income is always the sum of **expenditure** and **savings** (Income = Expenditure + Savings). Any increase in expenditure without a change in income directly reduces savings.

Annual Calculation Adjustments

When calculating **annual** values from monthly data, verify if any specific months have deviations or zero values due to special events like a **birthday celebration**.

Savings Percentage

The savings percentage can be calculated as (Monthly Savings ÷ Monthly Salary) × 100. In this case: (10,500 ÷ 17,000) × 100 ≈ 61.76%.

questions.question: A trader buys 20 kg of rice for ₹1,000. He sells the rice at the rate of ₹60 per kg. What is the percentage profit made by the trader?

[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

Ratio of **Cost Price (CP)** to **Selling Price (SP)** = 1000 : (20 × 60)

CP : SP = 1000 : 1200 = 5 : 6

Profit = 6 − 5 = 1 unit

**Profit %** = (1 ÷ 5) × 100 = 20%

**∴ The correct answer is 20%.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Selling Price (SP)** of 1 kg rice = ₹60

**Formula Used:**

Profit = Total SP − Total CP

Profit % = (Profit ÷ CP) × 100

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4a3dd5ca6046850fd5b3dfd6844a8d878c4ca634fa3fd2a11cdc95a1a89bdfd0.png] 

**Calculations:**

⇒ **Total Selling Price (SP)** = 20 × 60 = ₹1200

⇒ **Profit** = 1200 − 1000 = ₹200

⇒ **Profit %** = (200 ÷ 1000) × 100

⇒ **Profit %** = 20%

**∴ The correct answer is 20%.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Loss Percentage

When CP > SP, a loss occurs. Loss % = (Loss ÷ CP) × 100, where Loss = CP − SP.

Marked Price & Discount

Discount is a reduction offered on the **Marked Price (MP)**. SP = MP − Discount.

Profit Margin on SP

questions.question:
A hollow spherical shell is made of a metal of density 10 g/cm³. Its internal and external radius are 1 cm and 4 cm, respectively. What is the weight (in kg) of the shell?

(Use π = (22)/(7) and Density = (Mass)/(Volume) )
questions.solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

**Volume** of shell = 4/3 × π × (R³ − r³) = 4/3 × 22/7 × (4³ − 1³)

⇒ **Volume** = 4/3 × 22/7 × 63 = 4 × 22 × 3 = 264 cm³

**Mass** = Density × Volume = 10 × 264 = 2640 g

**Weight in kg** = 2640 ÷ 1000 = 2.64 kg

**∴ The correct answer is 2.64 kg.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

Metal **density** (ρ) = 10 g/cm³

**Internal radius** (r) = 1 cm

**External radius** (R) = 4 cm

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/da0900e345e7cb3b89ab09193a04908ec1a1fbb82837e3a93438e2e160bdcc92.png] 

**Formula Used:**

Volume of **hollow sphere** = 4/3 × π × (R³ − r³)

**Mass** = **Density** × **Volume**

**Calculations:**

⇒ Volume = 4/3 × 22/7 × (4³ − 1³)

⇒ Volume = 4/3 × 22/7 × (64 − 1)

⇒ Volume = 4/3 × 22/7 × 63

⇒ Volume = 4 × 22 × 3 = 264 cm³

⇒ Mass = 10 × 264 = 2640 g

⇒ Weight (in kg) = 2640 ÷ 1000 = 2.64 kg

**∴ The correct answer is 2.64 kg.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Volume of a Solid Sphere

The volume of a complete solid sphere is given by V = 4/3 × π × r³.

Surface Area of a Sphere

The total surface area of a sphere is 4 × π × r², and for a hollow shell, the total surface area is 4πR² + 4πr².

Unit Conversion

Always ensure units are consistent; 1 kg = 1000 g and 1 m³ = 10⁶ cm³.

questions.question: A recipe uses 2 cups of rice for every 3 cups of water. If you want to cook using 6 cups of rice, how much water will you need?
questions.solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

The **Ratio** of **Rice** to **Water** is 2 : 3.

Current **Rice** quantity = 6 cups, which is 3 **times** the original amount (6 ÷ 2 = 3).

To maintain the same **proportion**, multiply the **Water** quantity by the same factor: 3 × 3 = 9 cups.

**∴ The correct answer is 9 cups.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

Initial **Rice** (R₁) = 2 cups

Initial **Water** (W₁) = 3 cups

New **Rice** (R₂) = 6 cups

**Formula Used:**

Direct Proportion: R₁ / W₁ = R₂ / W₂

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/34ce6231e2b1db77b60cd37798797ea2ab63aaf99653fc666ee8b5020bff2250.png] 

**Calculations:**

⇒ 2 / 3 = 6 / W₂

⇒ 2 × W₂ = 6 × 3

⇒ 2 × W₂ = 18

⇒ W₂ = 18 ÷ 2

⇒ W₂ = 9

**∴ The correct answer is 9 cups.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Direct Proportion

Two quantities are in **direct proportion** if an increase in one leads to a corresponding increase in the other such that their ratio (x/y = k) remains constant.

Unitary Method

To solve using the **unitary method**, first find the amount of water needed for 1 cup of rice (3 ÷ 2 = 1.5) and then multiply by the desired amount (1.5 × 6 = 9).

Scaling Factor

The **scaling factor** is the constant multiplier used to increase or decrease both parts of a ratio simultaneously while maintaining the original relationship.
